albert-ludwigs-universitaet-freiburg.about:
The University of Freiburg is one of Germany's oldest universities and a member of the German U15 group of research universities. It covers eleven faculties, with notable strength in medicine, philosophy and history, biology, environment and natural resources, and microsystems engineering at its technical faculty.

International applicants apply online (medicine-related subjects via hochschulstart) and need a high level of German for most bachelor's programmes. As in all of Baden-Württemberg, non-EU/EEA students without a German entrance qualification pay an international tuition fee each semester on top of the semester fee.
albert-ludwigs-universitaet-freiburg.aid_intl: Some exemptions from international tuition; DAAD and Deutschlandstipendium (partial) scholarships.
albert-ludwigs-universitaet-freiburg.tests: No SAT/ACT. A high level of German is required for most undergraduate programmes (accepted certificates listed by the university). Applicants without direct university access attend a Studienkolleg. Medicine/dentistry/pharmacy are highly competitive.
albert-ludwigs-universitaet-freiburg.gpa_note: Restricted programmes select by converted school grade; medicine requires near-top grades.
requirements: University entrance qualification recognised in Germany (or Studienkolleg)
German proficiency certificate (e.g. DSH-2/TestDaF) for German-taught programmes
Proof of funds for the German student visa

beijing-institute-of-technology.about:
Beijing Institute of Technology (BIT), founded in 1940, is one of China's key engineering universities with historic roots in defence technology. It is strong in vehicle and mechanical engineering, aerospace, optics and photonics, information and electronics, and materials, and has campuses in Beijing (Zhongguancun, Liangxiang) and Zhuhai.

International undergraduates can choose Chinese-taught programmes (HSK) or a set of English-taught engineering and business programmes (TOEFL/IELTS), and must submit a CSCA report. CSC and university scholarships are available.
beijing-institute-of-technology.aid_intl: Chinese Government Scholarship (CSC) and university/provincial scholarships for international students; English-taught and self-funded programmes may have separate awards.
beijing-institute-of-technology.tests: From the 2026/27 intake every international undergraduate applicant to Chinese universities must submit a CSCA (China Scholastic Competency Assessment) report (national requirement run by the China Scholarship Council; tests held several times a year). Chinese-taught programmes require an HSK certificate (typically HSK 4–5 with 180+ depending on the major); English-taught programmes require TOEFL/IELTS or equivalent. SAT/ACT/IB/A-level results can support an application but are not required. Exact thresholds are set in the university's annual admissions guide.
beijing-institute-of-technology.gpa_note: Selection on senior-high record, language level, CSCA results and (where used) interview or written test.
requirements: High school diploma or expected graduation certificate
Interview or written test if required

beijing-normal-university.about:
Beijing Normal University (BNU) traces its history to 1902 and is China's flagship institution for education research and teacher preparation. It is also highly ranked in psychology, Chinese language and literature, history, geography and environmental science, with a second campus in Zhuhai.

International undergraduates usually study in Chinese (HSK required) and must provide a CSCA report; BNU is a popular choice for Chinese language and education degrees. CSC and Beijing Government scholarships are available.
beijing-normal-university.aid_intl: Chinese Government Scholarship (CSC) and university/provincial scholarships for international students; English-taught and self-funded programmes may have separate awards.
beijing-normal-university.tests: From the 2026/27 intake every international undergraduate applicant to Chinese universities must submit a CSCA (China Scholastic Competency Assessment) report (national requirement run by the China Scholarship Council; tests held several times a year). Chinese-taught programmes require an HSK certificate (typically HSK 4–5 with 180+ depending on the major); English-taught programmes require TOEFL/IELTS or equivalent. SAT/ACT/IB/A-level results can support an application but are not required. Exact thresholds are set in the university's annual admissions guide.
top_programs: Teaching Chinese to Speakers of Other Languages
beijing-normal-university.gpa_note: Selection on senior-high record, language level, CSCA results and (where used) interview or written test.
requirements: High school diploma or expected graduation certificate
Interview or written test if required

cardiff-university.about:
Founded in 1883, Cardiff University is a member of the Russell Group with a civic campus around Cathays Park in central Cardiff and a large medical campus at the University Hospital of Wales. It is known for its School of Journalism, Media and Culture, medicine, dentistry and healthcare, architecture (Welsh School of Architecture), psychology, and engineering.

International undergraduates apply through UCAS with predicted grades, a personal statement and a reference. The standard English requirement is IELTS 6.5 with 5.5 in each skill, and medicine and dentistry need the UCAT and an October deadline.
cardiff-university.aid_intl: Merit-based international scholarships (partial tuition discounts) for undergraduate entrants.
cardiff-university.tests: No SAT/ACT requirement in general (US applicants may use SAT/AP). English: GCSE English C/4 or IELTS Academic 6.5 overall with at least 5.5 in each skill (One Skill Retake accepted, IELTS Online not accepted); PTE Academic 69 is equivalent. Some courses ask for more. Medicine and dentistry require the UCAT.
cardiff-university.gpa_note: Typical offers range from ABB to A*AA at A-level (or IB equivalents) depending on the course.
requirements: English test (IELTS 6.5, min 5.5 per skill / PTE 69)
Proof of funds for the UK Student visa (CAS)

chalmers-university-of-technology.about:
Chalmers is a private foundation university (state-funded) founded in 1829, with Johanneberg and Lindholmen campuses in Gothenburg. It is known for engineering, architecture, materials, energy, transport and ICT research, and for close collaboration with Swedish industry.

Undergraduate engineering degrees (civilingenjör and högskoleingenjör) are taught in Swedish, so international students without Swedish usually join at master's level, where most teaching is in English. Applications go through universityadmissions.se, with the international round closing on 15 January.
chalmers-university-of-technology.aid_intl: Few or no bachelor's-level scholarships; Swedish Institute scholarships are for master's students. Some universities offer partial tuition waivers to fee-paying students.
chalmers-university-of-technology.tests: No SAT/ACT. Swedish-taught programmes require Swedish 3; English-taught programmes require English 6 (typically IELTS Academic 6.5 with no section below 5.5, or TOEFL iBT 90 with writing 20). Programme-specific maths/science prerequisites apply. Swedish-taught engineering programmes also require Swedish 3 plus advanced maths, physics and chemistry.
chalmers-university-of-technology.gpa_note: Selection mainly by upper-secondary grades (merit rating) when programmes are oversubscribed.
requirements: English 6 (e.g. IELTS 6.5 / TOEFL iBT 90) or Swedish 3, depending on the programme
Proof of funds for the Swedish residence permit

charles-university.about:
Charles University is the Czech Republic's largest and most prestigious university, with 17 faculties across Prague and in Hradec Králové and Plzeň. It is strong in medicine (five medical faculties), natural sciences, mathematics and physics, law, social sciences and the humanities.

International students choose between tuition-free Czech-language study and fee-paying English-taught programmes (notably general medicine, dentistry and selected social-science and humanities bachelor's). Applications go to individual faculties, typically by the end of February or March, with entrance exams and diploma recognition.
charles-university.aid_intl: Czech-taught study is free; limited faculty scholarships and Czech government scholarships for some countries.
charles-university.tests: No SAT/ACT. Most programmes use faculty entrance exams (some online), and foreign secondary diplomas need recognition (nostrification). English-taught programmes require proof of English; Czech-taught programmes require Czech. Medicine has its own entrance tests.
charles-university.gpa_note: Admission mainly through faculty entrance exam results; some programmes also weigh school grades.
requirements: Proof of funds for the Czech long-term visa

city-university-of-hong-kong-cityuhk.about:
City University of Hong Kong is a research university on a compact campus in Kowloon Tong. It has colleges of engineering, business, liberal arts and social sciences, science, computing, creative media and Hong Kong's only veterinary school, and is known for applied research and close ties with industry in the Greater Bay Area.

International applicants apply online as non-JUPAS candidates with their school-leaving results and English proficiency evidence. Teaching is entirely in English, and merit-based entrance scholarships are offered to strong non-local applicants.
city-university-of-hong-kong-cityuhk.aid_intl: Entrance scholarships for outstanding non-local students (partial to full tuition), awarded on merit.
city-university-of-hong-kong-cityuhk.tests: SAT/ACT may be used by applicants with US-curriculum qualifications; most international applicants are assessed on IB, A-level or national exam results. English proficiency (IELTS/TOEFL) is required for non-native speakers. Minimum scores could not be verified.
city-university-of-hong-kong-cityuhk.gpa_note: Competitive results in IB/A-level or equivalent are expected.
requirements: Secondary school results (IB, A-level, SAT/AP or national exams)
English test (IELTS/TOEFL) if not a native speaker

curtin-university.about:
Curtin University has its main Bentley campus in Perth plus campuses in Malaysia, Singapore, Dubai and Mauritius. Its Western Australian School of Mines is world-renowned, and it is also strong in earth sciences, petroleum and chemical engineering, business, health sciences, architecture and design.

International students apply online with their school results and English test scores at the course's level. Intakes are in February and July, and merit scholarships reduce tuition for high achievers.
curtin-university.aid_intl: Merit scholarships for international students (e.g. Curtin International Scholarships – Merit) offering partial tuition reductions.
curtin-university.tests: No SAT/ACT requirement in general; entry by secondary qualification against course requirements. English proficiency required per course (IELTS/TOEFL/PTE or equivalent); portfolio entry is available for some courses.
curtin-university.gpa_note: Course-specific minimum results for your qualification.
requirements: English test at the course's level
Proof of funds for the Australian student visa

dalhousie-university.about:
Founded in 1818, Dalhousie is a U15 research university with campuses in Halifax and an agricultural campus in Truro. It is particularly strong in ocean and marine sciences, medicine, dentistry, nursing and health professions, engineering, law (Schulich School of Law), management and architecture.

International students apply directly online; high-school grades and country-specific requirements drive admission, and SAT/ACT are not required. Applying by 15 February secures consideration for entrance awards, while health programmes and architecture have fixed deadlines.
dalhousie-university.aid_intl: Entrance scholarships for high-achieving applicants (apply by 15 Feb), plus the McCall MacBain international fellowship and other awards.
dalhousie-university.tests: SAT/ACT not required; admission is based on high-school grades and country-specific requirements. English proficiency required for non-native speakers (IELTS, TOEFL, CAEL, Duolingo or equivalent; minimums are listed on Dalhousie's requirements page).
dalhousie-university.gpa_note: Minimum grade averages by programme (typically 70%+; higher for health and engineering).
requirements: Supplemental requirements for some programmes (e.g. nursing, architecture, music)
Proof of funds for the Canadian study permit

friedrich-alexander-universitat-erlangen.about:
FAU, founded in 1743, is a large research university in Bavaria with five faculties and close ties to industry partners such as Siemens and Adidas. It is especially strong in engineering (including AI, electrical and mechanical engineering, materials science), medicine, the natural sciences and business and economics in Nuremberg.

International bachelor's applicants apply directly via FAU's campo portal; non-EU applicants for the summer semester apply from 2 November to 15 January. German proficiency is required for most programmes, and from summer semester 2027 FAU introduces tuition for non-EU students and a €100 application fee.
friedrich-alexander-universitat-erlangen.aid_intl: Germany-wide options such as DAAD scholarships and the Deutschlandstipendium (merit, partial); FAU fee exemptions in some cases.
friedrich-alexander-universitat-erlangen.tests: No SAT/ACT. Most bachelor's programmes are taught in German and require proof of German proficiency (e.g. DSH-2/TestDaF level). Applicants whose school certificate does not give direct university access need the Studienkolleg and its assessment test (Feststellungsprüfung). Medicine and some programmes are restricted.
friedrich-alexander-universitat-erlangen.gpa_note: Foreign grades are converted with the Bavarian formula; restricted programmes select by grade.
requirements: Higher education entrance qualification recognised in Germany (or Studienkolleg)
German proficiency (DSH-2/TestDaF level) for German-taught programmes
Blocked account/proof of funds for the German student visa

ghent-university.about:
Founded in 1817, Ghent University is a large Flemish public university with eleven faculties spread across the historic city of Ghent. It is internationally recognised for veterinary medicine, bioscience engineering, agriculture, pharmacy, medicine and engineering, and has a growing number of English-taught master's programmes.

At bachelor's level, however, every programme is taught in Dutch. International applicants apply online with a verified diploma, must show Dutch at B2 upon enrolment, and those needing a visa must apply before 1 April. Medicine-related degrees require the Flemish entrance exam.
ghent-university.aid_intl: Very limited for bachelor's students; most UGent scholarships target master's and PhD students from developing countries.
ghent-university.tests: No SAT/ACT. All UGent bachelor's programmes are taught in Dutch, and you need Dutch at B2 on enrolment (C1 for Applied Language Studies). Medicine, dentistry and veterinary medicine require passing the Flemish inter-university entrance exam with a favourable ranking; some programmes require a positioning test.
ghent-university.gpa_note: Open admission for holders of a recognised secondary diploma (plus proof of acceptance at a university at home for some countries); medicine is selective via the entrance exam.
requirements: Secondary school diploma verified through Qualification Check
Dutch B2 certificate (C1 for Applied Language Studies)
Flemish entrance exam for medicine/dentistry/veterinary medicine
Proof of funds for the Belgian student visa

harbin-institute-of-technology.about:
Harbin Institute of Technology (HIT), founded in 1920, is one of China's leading engineering universities, with its main campus in Harbin and branch campuses in Weihai and Shenzhen. It is a core institution for China's space programme and excels in aerospace, robotics, welding and materials, civil engineering and computing.

International undergraduates typically study in Chinese after meeting HSK requirements and submitting a CSCA report; some English-taught options exist. CSC scholarships are available.
harbin-institute-of-technology.aid_intl: Chinese Government Scholarship (CSC) and university/provincial scholarships for international students; English-taught and self-funded programmes may have separate awards.
harbin-institute-of-technology.tests: From the 2026/27 intake every international undergraduate applicant to Chinese universities must submit a CSCA (China Scholastic Competency Assessment) report (national requirement run by the China Scholarship Council; tests held several times a year). Chinese-taught programmes require an HSK certificate (typically HSK 4–5 with 180+ depending on the major); English-taught programmes require TOEFL/IELTS or equivalent. SAT/ACT/IB/A-level results can support an application but are not required. Exact thresholds are set in the university's annual admissions guide.
harbin-institute-of-technology.gpa_note: Selection on senior-high record, language level, CSCA results and (where used) interview or written test.
requirements: High school diploma or expected graduation certificate
Interview or written test if required

huazhong-university-of-science-and-techn.about:
HUST was formed in 1952 and merged with Tongji Medical University in 2000, creating one of China's largest research universities on a green campus in eastern Wuhan. It is renowned for the Wuhan National Laboratory for Optoelectronics, mechanical and electrical engineering, computing, and medicine.

International undergraduates apply online with school records, a CSCA report and HSK (or English scores for English-taught MBBS and engineering options). CSC and university scholarships are offered.
huazhong-university-of-science-and-techn.aid_intl: Chinese Government Scholarship (CSC) and university/provincial scholarships for international students; English-taught and self-funded programmes may have separate awards.
huazhong-university-of-science-and-techn.tests: From the 2026/27 intake every international undergraduate applicant to Chinese universities must submit a CSCA (China Scholastic Competency Assessment) report (national requirement run by the China Scholarship Council; tests held several times a year). Chinese-taught programmes require an HSK certificate (typically HSK 4–5 with 180+ depending on the major); English-taught programmes require TOEFL/IELTS or equivalent. SAT/ACT/IB/A-level results can support an application but are not required. Exact thresholds are set in the university's annual admissions guide.
huazhong-university-of-science-and-techn.gpa_note: Selection on senior-high record, language level, CSCA results and (where used) interview or written test.
requirements: High school diploma or expected graduation certificate
Interview or written test if required

korea-university.about:
Founded in 1905, Korea University is one of Korea's most prestigious private universities, with its Anam campus in north-east Seoul and a second campus in Sejong. It is particularly strong in business (Korea University Business School), law, political science and international studies (Division of International Studies), engineering, and medicine.

Foreign students apply through the international admission track for March or September entry, submitting school records, a study plan and Korean or English proficiency. Many programmes are Korean-taught, while the Division of International Studies and some business tracks teach in English.
korea-university.aid_intl: Merit scholarships for international students (admission scholarships covering part or all of tuition) and GKS government scholarships.
korea-university.tests: No SAT/ACT requirement (international results may be submitted as supporting evidence). Korean-taught programmes require TOPIK (usually level 3–4 or higher); English-taught tracks require TOEFL/IELTS or equivalent. Exact minimums are set in each semester's admission guideline.
korea-university.gpa_note: Holistic document review of school records and study plan; interviews for some programmes.
requirements: Passport and nationality documents of applicant and parents
Bank statement for the D-2 visa

linkoping-university.about:
Linköping University (LiU) was founded in 1975 and has campuses in Linköping, Norrköping and Stockholm (Solna). It pioneered interdisciplinary research themes and problem-based learning in medicine, and is strong in engineering, computer science, visualisation, materials and teacher education.

Most bachelor's programmes are taught in Swedish; international students without Swedish typically choose one of the English-taught bachelor's options or come for a master's. Applications are made through universityadmissions.se, with the first round closing on 15 January.
linkoping-university.aid_intl: Few or no bachelor's-level scholarships; Swedish Institute scholarships are for master's students. Some universities offer partial tuition waivers to fee-paying students.
linkoping-university.tests: No SAT/ACT. Swedish-taught programmes require Swedish 3; English-taught programmes require English 6 (typically IELTS Academic 6.5 with no section below 5.5, or TOEFL iBT 90 with writing 20). Programme-specific maths/science prerequisites apply.
linkoping-university.gpa_note: Selection mainly by upper-secondary grades (merit rating) when programmes are oversubscribed.
requirements: English 6 (e.g. IELTS 6.5 / TOEFL iBT 90) or Swedish 3, depending on the programme
Proof of funds for the Swedish residence permit
